A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Locally Compact Space|locally compact]] [[Definition:Hausdorff Space|Hausdorff space]], and $X^* = X \cup \set \infty$, with open sets the open sets of $X$ together with the sets $X^* \setminus K$ for [[Definition:Compact Subspace|compact]] $K \subseteq X$.
Then $X^*$ is a [[Definition:Compact Hausdorff Space|compact Hausdorff space]] containing $X$ as an open subspace.

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Riemann Sphere|Riemann sphere]] $\C \cup \set \infty$, with neighbourhoods of $\infty$ the sets $\set {\size z > R} \cup \set \infty$, is compact, and is homeomorphic to $\Bbb S^2$ by [[Definition:Stereographic Projection|stereographic projection]].

substitutions.the complement of a closed disk: the complement of a compact set
substitutions.C: an arbitrary locally compact Hausdorff space

object_map.reformulation: Replace complements of closed disks by complements of arbitrary compact sets.

validity_conditions: Hausdorffness of X makes compact sets closed, so the new open sets meet X in open sets.
Local compactness is exactly what separates points of X from infinity.
proof_plan:
Unions and finite intersections of the given sets are again of this form, as finite unions of compact sets are compact and $U \setminus K$ is open in $X$ for $K$ closed.
So $X^*$ is a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] with $X$ an open subspace.

Given an open cover of $X^*$, some member $X^* \setminus K$ contains $\infty$, and finitely many members cover the compact set $K$.
Hence $X^*$ is compact.

Points of $X$ are separated within $X$.
For $x \in X$, local compactness gives a compact neighbourhood $K$ of $x$, and $K^\circ$ and $X^* \setminus K$ separate $x$ from $\infty$.
